plan: Sell SOXL, SPAL, MUU, and METU to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce broad index concentration and meet single name limits.
Add to QQQI, targeting 25%, to favor income and stability.

conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a target of ~1.5%/month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces drawdown risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and concentrating on income and broad index holdings. Expect lower volatility and more stable returns, but also limited upside potential.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3%, SPAL to 2%, MUU to 3%, and METU to 2% to reduce overall leverage.
Trim SPY to 20% to meet single name concentration limits.
Buy DDOG at 4% as a strong scanner setup to add quality tech exposure.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining some exposure to high-quality tech.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5%/month, aiming for risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality tech name. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential, with a more diversified risk profile than the current book.

plan: Add to SOXL to 7%, MUU to 6%, METU to 6%, and SPAL to 6% to lean into leveraged ETFs.
Trim SPY to 20% to meet single name concentration limits.
Buy DDOG at 6% as a strong scanner setup to press what is working.
This plan aggressively seeks growth by increasing leveraged exposure and concentrating in high-scoring setups.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring scanner setups. Be aware this raises both upside and drawdown potential, leveraged ETFs decay daily, and it can lose a lot fast. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell SOXL, SPAL, MUU, and METU to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce broad index concentration and meet single name limits.
Add to QQQI, targeting 30%, to prioritize income and monthly distributions.

income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, prioritizing steady monthly distributions. It eliminates leveraged and high-beta single names, rotating into income-focused ETFs. While aiming for reliable income, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
